messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DIF and 3PL
parts:
I'm not quite sure I understand. If you want 3PL models in multipleGroup(), just pass itemtype = '3PL' and all the items will be estimated using that model. The DIF() function is agnostic to the type of model run, so you would just need to specify which parameters should  be constrained/freed to test for DIF. If that doesn't make sense, try attaching some code so we can see how far along you are. Cheers.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: DIF and 3PL
parts:
Thanks for your quick response Phil!

I passed itemtype='3PL' in multiplegroup() as you suggested. It worked exactly like you stated. If you have the time I'd love for a check of the syntax to make sure I'm on the right track.

For reference my data is a  20 item verbal and 20 item math dichotomous test taken by 318 participants in two different circumstances. Because the assessment is a test, I would like to use the 3PL model, as I stated before. I would like to see if the context of the test affects the results.

My syntax was largely copied from your example, it is as follows:

library("mirt") #loads the mirt package


mathmobile<-read.csv("C:/XXX/CAMobileMath.csv")
mathlab<-read.csv("C:/XXXCALabMath.csv")
verbalmobile<-read.csv("C:/XXX/CAMobileVerbal.csv")
verballab<-read.csv("C:/XXX/CALabVerbal.csv")

combinedmath<-rbind(mathmobile, mathlab)
group <- c(rep('D1', 318,), rep('D2', 318))

combinedverbal<-rbind(verbalmobile,verballab)
group <- c(rep('D1', 318,), rep('D2',318))

mirtCluster()

#  Information matrix with S-EM
modelmath <- multipleGroup(combinedmath,1, itemtype='3PL', group, SE = TRUE)
modelverbal <- multipleGroup(combinedverbal,1, itemtype='3PL', group, SE = TRUE)

#test whether adding slopes and intercepts constraints results in DIF. Plot items showing DIF
resulta1dmath <- DIF(modelmath, c('a1', 'd'),plotdif = TRUE)
resulta1dmath
resulta1dverbal<-DIF(modelverbal,c('a1','d'),plotdif = TRUE)
resulta1dverbal

#same as above, but using Wald tests with Benjamini & Hochberg adjustment
resulta1dWaldmath <- DIF(modelmath, c('a1', 'd'), Wald = TRUE, p.adjust = 'fdr')
resulta1dWaldmath
round(resulta1dWaldmath$adj_pvals, 4)

resulta1dWaldverbal <- DIF(modelverbal, c('a1', 'd'), Wald = TRUE, p.adjust = 'fdr')
resulta1dWaldverbal
round(resulta1dWaldverbal$adj_pvals, 4)

#test whether adding only slope constraints results in DIF for all items
resulta1math <- DIF(modelmath, 'a1',plotdif=TRUE)
resulta1math
resultdmath <- DIF(modelmath,'d', plotdif=TRUE)
resultdmath
resulta1verbal <- DIF(modelverbal, 'a1',plotdif=TRUE)
resulta1math
resultdmath <- DIF(modelverbal,'d', plotdif=TRUE)
resultdverbal
#End

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DIF and 3PL
parts:
In theory a lot of this is fine, but for DIF it's better to free the latent mean and variance of the focal groups to adjust for overall group differences. You'll need to select a set of anchor items, set their parameters equal across groups, and add the invariance = c('free_means', 'free_var') argument to multipleGroup(). Try to follow the examples in help(DIF) because they properly set up the metric for DIF testing. 

As for the code, I think it's okay. You are essentially performing a 2 df DIF test for the slope and intercept parameters and leaving the g parameters equal across groups (which makes sense, testing for DIF in the g's would require a massive sample size). My only issue is that, given your current sample size, the 3PL model will be pretty unstable and probably give bad estimates for the g parameters. I'd recommend either putting a strong prior on the g's, or simply set them all equal to some reasonable constant (like guess = 0.2, if there are 5 response options for each item, and then just use the itemtype = '2PL' argument). Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DIF and 3PL
parts:
You could still use the 2PL model to perform DIF testing, as the two are equivalent asymptotically (SEM is really a 3-stage approximation to what IRT does for DIF testing, but it generally useful if the dimensionality of the latent trait model grows too large, or there are other structural interests like predicting external variables). Cheers.

Phil
